432: ## S1896 (2026-11-01): the identity's representable open immersion is constructible; the D9 cusp is not
433: 
434: **Result.** `tmp/sheaf/xif/paper/S1896BoundaryCuspActual.lean` (EXIT=0, axioms
435: propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound, source SHA256 B69D9E5F...46BE2, olean SHA256
436: 6999EEF2...9AD1) constructs the **first inhabitant in the tree of
437: `Iut.EtaleStackRepresentableMorphismProperty`**: for every etale stack `Y` the
438: identity `𝟙 Y.fiber` is representably an open immersion
439: (`S1896IdentityOpenImmersion`), with a full `TwoPullbackWitness` whose apex is the
440: test scheme itself (the actual 2-pullback of `(𝟙, point)`, S1804's "apex = the
441: scheme" model).  It also localises the D9 cusp exactly as
442: (compactification stack, representable open immersion, boundary point)
443: (`S1896FirstMissing_structure`), and proves the identity open map is **never** a
444: cusp's open map (`S1896Id_not_boundary`, `S1896Cusp_openMap_app_not_essSurj`).
445: 
446: **New research fact.** The obstruction to the D9 cusp is *not* the 2-pullback /
447: representability machinery: that machinery is now known to be inhabitated and to be
448: discharged by unitors and the exchange law alone.  The obstruction is the geometric
449: compactification of `S.cK` (a stack strictly extending it, with an open immersion
450: that is not levelwise essentially surjective at the boundary point).  S1887's
451: "no inhabitant of the property type exists" is superseded; what remains is the
452: compactification choice, downstream of the still-missing `S1881D9OrbicurveMissing`.
453: 
454: **Engineering fact (reusable, cost several compile cycles).** On
455: `Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans X Y` two *definitionally equal but syntactically
456: different* `Category` instances coexist (`EtaleStackPseudofunctor.homCategory`,
457: global, in `Iut/Foundations/Orbicurve.lean`, and mathlib's scoped
458: `Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans.homCategory`).  As a result `Bicategory.whisker_exchange`,
459: `whiskerRight_id`, `whiskerRight_iff`, `whiskerLeftIso`, `rightUnitor` do **not**
460: elaborate directly at `EtaleStackPseudofunctor F` (the hom-type metavariables stay
461: unsolved).  Recipe: wrap through `let Bicat := EtaleStackPseudofunctor F;
462: letI : Bicategory Bicat := inferInstance` and `exact @Bicategory.<lemma> Bicat _ ...`
463: (the S1756 pattern), generalised to an arbitrary field in S1896 §0.  Second trap:
464: after `simp only [Category.assoc]` a mixed-instance 2-cell equation can remain, and
465: `rfl` closes it.  Any future open-immersion / finite-etale representability package
466: should start from `S1896WhiskerLeftIso`, `S1896WhiskerRightIso`, `S1896LeftUnitorIso`,
467: `S1896RightUnitorIso`, `S1896WhiskerRightId`, `S1896WhiskerExchange`,
468: `S1896WhiskerRightIff`, `S1896Modification_subsingleton`.

439  (`S1896IdentityOpenImmersion`), with a full `TwoPullbackWitness` whose apex is the
440  test scheme itself (the actual 2-pullback of `(𝟙, point)`, S1804's "apex = the
441  scheme" model).  It also localises the D9 cusp exactly as
442  (compactification stack, representable open immersion, boundary point)
443  (`S1896FirstMissing_structure`), and proves the identity open map is **never** a
444  cusp's open map (`S1896Id_not_boundary`, `S1896Cusp_openMap_app_not_essSurj`).

446  **New research fact.** The obstruction to the D9 cusp is *not* the 2-pullback /
447  representability machinery: that machinery is now known to be inhabitated and to be
448  discharged by unitors and the exchange law alone.  The obstruction is the geometric
449  compactification of `S.cK` (a stack strictly extending it, with an open immersion
450  that is not levelwise essentially surjective at the boundary point).  S1887's
451  "no inhabitant of the property type exists" is superseded; what remains is the
452  compactification choice, downstream of the still-missing `S1881D9OrbicurveMissing`.

455  `Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans X Y` two *definitionally equal but syntactically
456  different* `Category` instances coexist (`EtaleStackPseudofunctor.homCategory`,
457  global, in `Iut/Foundations/Orbicurve.lean`, and mathlib's scoped
458  `Pseudofunctor.StrongTrans.homCategory`).  As a result `Bicategory.whisker_exchange`,
459  `whiskerRight_id`, `whiskerRight_iff`, `whiskerLeftIso`, `rightUnitor` do **not**
460  elaborate directly at `EtaleStackPseudofunctor F` (the hom-type metavariables stay
461  unsolved).  Recipe: wrap through `let Bicat := EtaleStackPseudofunctor F;
462  letI : Bicategory Bicat := inferInstance` and `exact @Bicategory.<lemma> Bicat _ ...`
463  (the S1756 pattern), generalised to an arbitrary field in S1896 §0.  Second trap:
464  after `simp only [Category.assoc]` a mixed-instance 2-cell equation can remain, and
465  `rfl` closes it.  Any future open-immersion / finite-etale representability package
